it-2006-cs-23.approach: Test each identity region by region (the 8 Venn regions of $P,Q,R$): an identity holds iff both sides contain exactly the same regions. One counter-region kills statement 1; statement 2 is the distributive law of $\cap$ over $\Delta$.

steps.title: Statement 1 fails
steps.body:
Take an element $x \in Q$, $x \notin P$, $x \notin R$.

- LHS: $x \in Q \cup R$ and $x \notin P$, so $x \in P \Delta (Q \cup R)$.
- RHS: $x \in P \Delta Q$ (in $Q$ only) but $x \notin P \Delta R$ (in neither), so $x \notin (P\Delta Q) \cap (P \Delta R)$.

The two sides differ, so 1 is FALSE.

steps.title: Statement 2 holds
steps.body:
Membership of $x$ in $Q \Delta R$ is $q \oplus r$. Then

$$x \in P \cap (Q \Delta R) \iff p \wedge (q \oplus r) = (p\wedge q) \oplus (p \wedge r) \iff x \in (P\cap Q)\Delta(P \cap R)$$

since AND distributes over XOR. So 2 is TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Only statement 2 is true, which is option B.
